Widening the split books more of what was asked; it removes nothing.

decisions.summary: A phase ties to the run of its session whose span holds it and whose target is its make OR whose task is its task, ranked target, then task, then latest start; unmatched phases counted in the footnote, never dropped; a phase starting after the window is none of it.
decisions.why: D4 ties by session, clone and target; adding task as a second key moved 567 untied compile phases (60.9 min) to 170 (12.1 min), measured, so it brings more of the GM's compile time under its task (the per-task breakdown he asked for). It narrows nothing. Note for the caller: the block's restatement omits D4's clone key; since builders share the main session's id (D4), dropping clone could tie a phase to a same-task or same-target run in another clone. Not ruled on - the block is silent, not explicit - but confirm the code still keys on clone.

decisions.summary: A background run ends at the main transcript's queue-operation enqueue row naming its tool-use-id, before its BgEnd line's t.
decisions.why: D3 itself says a BgEnd's t is when the notice reached the session, not when the run ended (the notice waits while the session is mid-turn); the enqueue row is the nearer reading of the run's own end. More accurate booking of what was asked; nothing dropped - BgEnd remains the fallback.

decisions.summary: A background run with no enqueue row or BgEnd ends at the TaskStop call that stopped it (read from the session's and its subagents' transcripts), else open to the window's end.
decisions.why: A stopped run has ended; booking it open to the window's end was a wrong outcome (ten runs, 6,070 of 6,792 machine minutes booked 'other', measured). D3's 'open to the window's end' is the fallback for a launch with no end anywhere, and a TaskStop is an end. Adds an end source; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A subagent's call inside the main session's turn is booked on the critical path as what the session was doing (the call it waits on, or the model); between turns it keeps the wait open. The session's own line moves state before a zero gap is skipped, and SubagentStart/SubagentStop keep it.
decisions.why: D7 defines the critical path as the wall clock partitioned by what the MAIN SESSION was doing or waiting on; a builder's line cutting the session's make static in two misbooked the session's own state. This implements D7 literally; builder runs are still booked in the runs table (machine minutes).

decisions.summary: A call running several targets is booked by the first of them in PRECEDENCE (land, gate, tests, review, docs, spec-kit step, other) in both tables; a phase ties to a run that runs its make at all; a landing's gate and cohort phases are split out as gate, less the compile inside them.
decisions.why: FR-001/D2 book a call by its target and are silent on a line with several; the day's 19 landings were launched 'make claims-owed ...; make ledger-owed; make land' and booked review by their first target, which misses the land and gate columns FR-005 asks for (land 4.2, gate 0.0 against 27.4 min of their own gate phases, measured). The block's own cross-check (land 5.3 + gate 14.4 + compile 13.0 = 32.7 min against the end phases' 32.4) shows precedence absorbs almost no non-land time. Cohort booked as gate follows D5 (cohort-landing is the landing's gate stage).

decisions.summary: where-time shows a critical-path (wall clock) table and a runs table of every session's and agent's Bash calls in overlapping machine minutes, never summed into the wall clock.
decisions.why: D7 asks for the critical path 'and beside it the summed agent-minutes'; FR-005 'the wall clock on the critical path apart from the summed agent-minutes'. The runs table is that.

decisions.summary: UNTIL= passes --until (held Makefile edited); logs read to their end so a run still going at UNTIL is clipped there, not dropped.
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask for UNTIL=; clipping rather than dropping keeps the run's in-window time booked.

decisions.summary: 159 compile and landing-gate phases (9.5 min) tie to no run; left, counted and shown in the runs table's footnote, ruled 'not a defect'.
decisions.why: The time is shown, not lost: the GM's 'how much time recompiling' is answered with the footnote. No reader is told a wrong number; per WHAT A DEFECT IS, a gap counted and displayed is not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: feature-report is held unchanged here; its reading of the columns is T11's.
decisions.why: A task split inside the feature, not a removal: FR-005/D7 still require feature-report to read the same columns through the same functions, and the block assigns it to T11 rather than dropping it. Not verifiable from the bundle that T11's line carries it; the caller should confirm.

decisions.summary: A subagent's background run whose notice reached only its own transcript (the queued_command attachment) ends here at BgEnd, TaskStop or the window's end; reading queued_command is deferred to T09, lands before T10.
decisions.why: D3 says 'The readers (T08) ... read the subagent transcript's queued_command attachment', so this narrows T08 against D3's own wording. It is legitimate as a task-ordering narrowing only: the requirement stays in the feature (FR-002/D3), the block gives the why (D3's end-of-run work is T09's), the filed task and the order ('lands before T10') as FR-009 requires, and T09 is the very next task on the same reader. The GM's request sets no task order that this breaks, and the defect is not carried past the reader work. Not verifiable from the bundle that T09's section names it; the caller should confirm before ticking T09.

decisions.summary: The critical path still books 866 of 1,354 min 'waiting on work'; booking a wait to the runs in flight (D3, the FR-005/D7 'background run' column) is deferred to T09 and the critical path apart from the agents to T10; filed as T09, lands before T10.
decisions.why: This is the spec's headline wrong (SC-001: under a tenth unexplained; today 64%), so it is a narrowing of T08 and not a 'within'. It is legitimate on the same footing as the queued_command deferral: FR-002 and D3 assign wait-to-run booking a mechanism of its own (inflight on the Stop, else the holding launch), the block names the owner (T09, then T10 for D7's agent split) and the order, and the requirement and its success criterion are untouched. It also covers the 'background run' column FR-005 lists, which neither table carries yet. The deferral is legitimate only if T09 lands before any non-reader work; a spec where SC-001 is not met at the close would be a defect, not this.

decisions.summary: The critical path's model column (342 min) holds about 235.4 min between turns, because a turn's Stop line often lands in 449's log and the 451 walk never sees the turn end; reading a session's turn lines from every feature's log is folded into T10 (D5, D6), lands before T11. Two smaller wrongs the same check found (a builder's stop inside make static; the zero-gap skip) are fixed here.
decisions.why: A known wrong outcome left standing (model minutes booked that are really the session waiting), so a narrowing. Legitimate because the fix needs a decision that belongs to the critical-path design T10 owns (how a turn spent on another feature is booked against this feature's wall clock - D7's critical path apart from the agents), the block states why, the task and the order (before T11) as FR-009 requires, the smaller wrongs reachable inside T08 were fixed here, and the requirement stays in the feature. Not verifiable from the bundle that T10's task line carries it (the caller says it does). Ordering seam for the caller: T09's wait booking keys on the Stop that opened a wait, and those are the very Stop lines this item says land in 449's log; T09 should read them across logs or know T10 will, else T09's numbers are built on the same missing lines.

decisions.summary: A launch paired with its BgEnd, else the subagent transcript's queued_command row holding its tool-use-id, else open to the window's end; a wait booked to the runs its Stop names inflight, else to the launch whose span holds it (a Stop written before the field: the session's own runs/agents whose span holds the gap).
decisions.why: D3's reader half as written.

decisions.summary: Stop and UserPromptSubmit lines of the window's sessions read from every feature's log, kept once; a foreign Stop/prompt taken as 451's only when a line of the session's own lies between it and its paired line, else marked events::FOREIGN.
decisions.why: FR-002/D3 book a between-turns wait from the Stop that opened it; a misfiled Stop is otherwise invisible. Taking a foreign turn only when it holds 451's own lines keeps 449's turns out of 451's model. How the requested booking happens, not added scope.

decisions.summary: A left-out foreign turn books from its prompt to the session's next line of 451's own to a new column 'another feature' (247 min in T08's window), the waits between 449's turns among it, moving no state of 451's walk.
decisions.why: D7 partitions the critical path by what the main session was DOING or waiting on; while it worked 449's turns it was doing another feature, so that time is not 451's model, idle or waits, and showing it as its own column keeps it visible rather than hiding it - 'where our time went on that task' answered without crediting 451 with 449's work. This is the cure of last round's NOT LEGITIMATE item, applied window-wide: the column also takes minutes that had sat in model, in 'none', and with a 451 agent in flight (the agent share fell 945 -> 864, none 147 -> 3); that is consistent, since the session in those minutes was on 449's turns, not waiting on 451's agent. A column beyond FR-005's list is within, as T08's plan review/other subagent/idle columns are: D7's partition needs a bucket for it.

decisions.summary: SubagentStart/SubagentStop lines read from every log as the turn lines are; an agent counts for the feature only where a line of its own log names it.
decisions.why: D3 books a wait to the agents inflight names and an agent's span needs its start and stop lines (9 of 115 had their start only in 449's log, measured); the own-log filter keeps 449's agents off 451's waits. Inside D3.

decisions.summary: With several runs in flight each second goes to one run by rank (named Bash column in PRECEDENCE order, agent, unnamed Bash 'background run', monitor; latest started breaks a tie); a Bash second splits into compile/gate as a call's does; an agent's second to its foreground-wait column; a second no run holds stays waiting on work; waits printed by holder.
decisions.why: D7's partition books each second once; D3 is silent on the split, so the order is design inside what was asked. The by-holder footnote serves the unexplained-waiting measure.

decisions.summary: the_columns_book_make_runs_compile_and_until's no-inflight wait now books 5 min land and 7 min none instead of 12 min waiting on work.
decisions.why: The intended effect of FR-002 on a pinned fixture.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] under FR-013's measurement clause; the command 1.16-1.24 s -> 1.58-1.90 s wall, measured.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts where-time's readers as performance work for ordering. The slower command is a measured cost, not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: The between-turn model minutes T10's line names are fixed here (model 342 -> 89); T10 keeps agent-minutes, tokens and rework, reading turn ends through events::turn_lines. The 253-vs-235.4 gap reconciled: 15.1 of the 18 min inside 449's own turns now booked another feature, 2.9 stated unreconciled, method given.
decisions.why: Pulling work forward into the walk that books both is inside FR-005; the reconciliation asked for last round is now in the block, and a stated 2.9 min residue is not a defect left. Text to correct (not a narrowing): this bullet still says the 253 moved 'to the waits', but by the section's own tables waits rose only ~866 -> ~994 and the rest went to 'another feature'; and the Measured footnote's 992 min of waits disagrees with its own parts (120+864+9+3 = 996) and with the wait columns (994, 996 with review) by more than rounding.

decisions.summary: Idle 126 -> 0: the two stretches over an hour (08:32-09:35Z, 10:42-11:46Z) the session spent on 449's turns now book 'another feature' (123 min) and model (4 min), measured per stretch, with a red test (a_stop_in_another_features_log_opens_the_wait, red2/red3).
decisions.why: Last round's NOT LEGITIMATE item fixed in T09 as the cure prescribed: the session's time on another feature's turns is booked apart rather than to 451's runs or none, red first. Nothing is left, so no ruling is owed.

decisions.summary: A first SubagentStart with no meta file is filed by the Agent call that dispatched it (per-session side file <events dir>-dispatches/<sid>.jsonl), else by the session's unreturned calls of its type within WINDOW_S (300 s, GUESS), only where every candidate's brief agrees; a disagreement stays feature.json's, marked.
decisions.why: Booking each agent's time to the feature and task it served is the per-task breakdown the GM asked for (2026-11-19) and measurement work FR-013 counts as performance work; an agreed-only rule leaves the undecidable case marked rather than wrong. FIFO dropped on measured inversions is design, not scope.

decisions.summary: A command's F= with no T= of its own no longer overrides the brief's task; the brief wins unless the command carries its own T=, matching the re-file's BY BRIEF rule; a decision against T26's stated order.
decisions.why: T26's order was a plan decision, not the GM's words; reversing it so a builder's time is booked to the task its brief served implements the request's per-task breakdown more faithfully. Nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: filed.rs and fields.rs read F= and T= from strip_heredocs of the command, never from text quoted inside a heredoc; a quoted F="451" stays the command's own.
decisions.why: Fixes a measured wrong filing (lines booked to 385 from quoted test code); serves the per-task breakdown.

decisions.summary: A task-only brief is not matched to a task start more than 72 h (GUESS) before the line; such a line falls to feature.json's feature, marked fallback.
decisions.why: Fixes the measured 23-line misfiling into 385's log; a marked fallback is kept apart by readers, so the outcome moves from wrong to unattributed. Knob labeled GUESS with its distribution measured.

decisions.summary: rust/gate/crates/measure (T09's) is not edited; the writer converges on the re-file's rule instead.
decisions.why: Coordination between two tasks of the same feature; no part of the request is narrowed by it.

decisions.id: T53-6 the 23 written lines deferred to T56
decisions.summary: The 23 lines already written into 385's log are not moved here; filed as T56 (the re-file sharing the writer's stale-start rule), lands before T22, because the re-file lives in the crate T09 is editing.
decisions.why: The defect is not dropped from the feature: it is filed with an id, a reason and an order (FR-009's three parts), and the writer's fix that stops new such lines lands here. Sequencing a fix within the same feature to a filed task is not a narrowing of what the GM asked. Note: T56 must actually move them, since they are misbooked time.

decisions.id: T53-7 older past-72h briefs in closed features
decisions.summary: 444's T42 (313 h) and 417's T46 (618 h) task-only lines left as they are; not shown to be wrong; the re-file does not reach those closed features.
decisions.why: Not a shown wrong outcome in closed features, and the request's reproducibility target (SC-002) is for work after landing; leaving an unshown difference is within per the 2026-11-19 defect rule.

decisions.id: T53-8 nested task-only brief now fallback
decisions.summary: A nested subagent whose brief names only a task and whose clone holds no fresh start of it is filed under feature.json's feature marked fallback, rather than by a stale start.
decisions.why: Moves such lines from booked-wrong to marked-and-kept-apart; nothing is booked wrong, and the common case (a fresh start, p90 1.8 h) still resolves to its task. An unattributed gap is not a wrong outcome under the defect rule.

decisions.id: T53-9 done measures and landing owe
decisions.summary: Red-first tests per shape, 702 passing; the dry run still moves 21 until the landing's live binary updates; one real events-refile owed at landing at the coordinator's timing, then a dry run showing 0 to move but the 23.
decisions.why: Verification of the requested data's correctness; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: One appended side-file line per Agent call half (about 150 bytes) and at most one 64 KiB tail read (TAIL, GUESS) at a meta-less first start; the hook never refuses or prints.
decisions.why: Design cost, not fidelity; keeps T26's constraints.

decisions.summary: Each agent's tokens are read from its agent-<aid>.jsonl usage rows inside the window, each message.id once, and the last SubagentStop tok is used only where no transcript row counts (a declared departure from D6's 'the reader keeps the last per aid').
decisions.why: Following the letter would defeat the request's purpose, which is an agent's token cost. By the block's own dated figures the stop's tok is short of the transcript rows on 16 of the 17 stops that carry one, and only 17 of 279 stops carry one, so reading it would report wrong costs. The stop line is still read as the fallback, so the request's 'read those new lines' and its cheap-history purpose survive for agents whose transcripts are gone. The writer defect is filed as T59 with why, id and order. Not settled from the bundle: whether the 262 stops with no tok at all are the same writer defect (T59 should cover an absent tok as well as a short one).

decisions.summary: Each agent is kept once with its kind and its task (first start's task from the launch brief per D6, else its first stop's) and booked by start to the task its lines name, or by tick to the mark at its first start. The old walk, which read only the 451 log and booked by the mark, is deleted.
decisions.why: D7 says 'each agent's span and tokens under its task', and D6 says where an agent's task comes from. It is read from every feature's log through T09's single build of the spans, as the dispatch states.

decisions.summary: Agent spans are cut to SINCE/UNTIL, overlapping spans are merged (a double start with no stop between counts once), an agent with nothing left is dropped, and token rows are limited to the window. The clip applies to the flight's agents only, so the time table is untouched.
decisions.why: D7 reports the window's wall clock with the agent-minutes beside it, so the agent-minutes are the window's. The dispatch names the clip and the single count of a double start, and the time table is measured unchanged line for line.

decisions.summary: A refused landing is a landing end line whose landed is false, never read from its exit code. A landing of several tasks is one refusal, counted under each task.
decisions.why: This is D7's and D5's definition word for word: 'landed is false', and 'exit 3 with its ticks standing is a landing whatever its code'.

decisions.summary: A plan re-round is any spec-fidelity or spec-fidelity-verify agent of a task after its first, each agent counted once (a resume is not a new round), with an agent naming no task counted as no task's re-round. The count therefore includes every spec-fidelity review dispatched under the task, not just its plan's rounds: 68 in the window, about 3x the feature report's 23 rounds past the first.
decisions.why: This is D7's parenthetical word for word: 'a task's spec-fidelity and spec-fidelity-verify dispatches after its first'. The request asks for no re-round count of its own, so the block narrows no clause. The block measures and discloses the 3x against the feature report's rounds-per-subject table, which is a different quantity. Whether D7's label 'plan re-rounds' overstates its own definition is a question about the spec, not this block.

decisions.summary: After the time table, where-time prints a by-task table (agents, agent minutes, k tokens in, k tokens out, refused landings, plan re-rounds, kinds) with an all row, a row per agent under its task, and a line setting the agents' summed minutes beside the critical path's wall clock. feature-report is wired by T11.
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask for the critical path's wall clock apart from the summed agent-minutes, each agent's span and tokens under its task, and the rework counts. This is that output.

decisions.summary: The critical path, the turn ends and the between-turn model minutes are T09's and are restated, not rebuilt. The 2.5 min left unreconciled is not traced further.
decisions.why: The dispatch says T09's work is restated. The time table is measured unchanged, and an untraced 2.5 min (under 1%) is a difference, not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: The SubagentStop writer's short tok is not fixed in T10. It is filed as T59, to land before T22, because the writer is the guard's file, outside T10.
decisions.why: T10 is FR-005's reader. The writer defect is FR-004's and is fixed in this feature by T59, which carries FR-009's why, id and order. The reader routes around it meanwhile, so no wrong number reaches the report.

decisions.summary: The -0 minutes printed for a task row with no agent is fixed by folding the sums from 0.0, with a red-first pin.
decisions.why: A defect found and fixed in the task.

decisions.summary: The 12 agents (94 min) that name no task stay under no task.
decisions.why: FR-004 gives an agent a task 'where its dispatch names one', so an agent whose dispatch names none has none to be booked under.

decisions.summary: make closing-checks starts make static, make hooks-test and make quick at once, one combined verdict, per-check logs, exit 1 if any red, TERM/INT stops all three; FRESH/REASON/HOOKS_ALL passed through
decisions.why: The performance task the GM asked to be filed on 2026-11-21 ('yes please file that as a performance task'), [perf] under FR-013.

decisions.summary: the last 25 lines of each red check's log are printed (a GUESS)
decisions.why: An output detail of the requested target, labeled a GUESS.

decisions.summary: static_runs_hooks counts a make closing-checks as one make static run; STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK stays 2
decisions.why: Stops the new target being used to get round FR-007/D11's count. It enforces what was already asked and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the event log books make closing-checks to tests (BUCKETS)
decisions.why: FR-001's one shared table, extended to the new target.

decisions.summary: the root CLAUDE.md's verification list states the order in one line
decisions.why: Documentation of the order. The refusal is the enforcement and this line carries none.

decisions.summary: the order at make decide (a decide after the caller's last code edit with no closing-checks started after it) is a NOTICE, not a refusal
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last round, which ruled it LEGITIMATE. A refusal at decide time cannot tell the closing tail from a decide in mid-build, because that depends on code edits that have not happened yet. The replay has 30 of 75 firings wrong (40%). Refusing anyway would force a closing-checks run on unfinished code, and that run counts toward FR-007's STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK=2, which defeats the performance purpose.

decisions.summary: a foreground make static, make hooks-test or make closing-checks (chained, piped, under timeout, the main session's) is REFUSED, red first, naming run_in_background and make closing-checks, recorded blocked; escaped by FOREGROUND_OK="<reason>" (recorded escaped, a bare token refused); STATIC_OK does not stand it aside; judged on every command of a chain before the decide notice; both refusals heard at once
decisions.why: This is the fix the last round asked for. The rule is now real enforcement in D12's form, carries FR-012's red-first test (708 passed, 3 failed on a stub; the suite's case 9 at 26 passed, 8 failed; then green at 711 and 34/34), and has a recorded escape for the cases where it is wrong. For static and hooks-test, the separate replay the last round asked for was done and stated in words: 55 foreground calls (27+28), 5 on correct work (4+1), 50 right (34 after the last edit + 16 mid-build; 19+9+6 and 11+5). That is 9%, set against the decide rule's 40%, and no FR-007 collision, because a backgrounded run is the same one static run. The arithmetic checks. A refusal implements the requested order. It is not a narrowing of it. Refusing make closing-checks rests on the earlier ruling, which is acceptable because the log has no foreground call of it to replay.

decisions.summary: a foreground make quick, the third closing check, is not refused (implicit: the refusal names static, hooks-test and closing-checks only)
decisions.why: The block does not label this, but it is a decision. The finding's cost is the slow checks run in the foreground one after another, and quick takes 1 to 5 s (item 9's timings). By item 4's own counts, the 51 foreground closing-check calls after the last edit (35.0 min) less the replay's 34 static/hooks-test calls (31.2 min) leave about 17 calls and about 4 min for quick. Inside closing-checks, quick already runs beside the others. Not refusing it does not gut the purpose. The decide notice still tells the order, and the slow checks are enforced by refusal.

decisions.summary: the refusal of a foreground make closing-checks is not replayed (no PreToolUse line names it) and rests on the plan review's ruling
decisions.why: Nothing could be measured because the target did not exist in the log. The refusal is the stricter side of the request, and T22 reads its blocked and escaped rows.

decisions.summary: a code edit made by a Bash write (sed -i, heredoc) is not seen by the decide notice: it can miss, never wrongly fire
decisions.why: A stated limit of a notice that has already been ruled legitimate. It refuses nothing, and the foreground refusal does not depend on it.

decisions.summary: the closing tail's idle minutes on later tasks' transcripts, the notice's noticed rows, and the refusal's blocked and escaped rows are read on T22's measured day; the mechanism's own before/after (104 s in sequence vs 52 s at once) is measured now
decisions.why: The effect in the world can only be read from transcripts of tasks that do not exist yet. The mechanism's own before/after is measured in the block, and T22 is the close's measured day that FR-013 names. The line now covers the refusal's blocked and escaped rows as well. The same caveat applies as last round: T22's own text is not in this bundle, so the session has to confirm that T22 takes these rows.

decisions.summary: item 4's recount: 93 calls by 38 builders after their last code edit, 51 foreground (35.0 min), 39 background, 3 refused by other guards; 28 builders decided after their last edit, 21 before any check; the earlier 92/56/33 reading explained
decisions.why: A restated measurement, not a decision about scope. 51+39+3=93. The difference from the first reading is put down to the pre-T04 bg rule and to the log having grown.

decisions.summary: make static is left unchanged because its Phase lines show it builds and runs no plain test; the double build is moved to where it actually happens, make rust-test after a green coverage pass, by widening T111's keep
decisions.why: The task line asked for static's plain build and test to be dropped. Measured Phase lines (dated, per target) show static has neither, so dropping one is impossible. The plan goes after the duplication the line was about (a crate's tests built in rust-test and again in coverage), which serves the GM's perf-first ordering (request.md 2026-11-20/21).

decisions.summary: a binary is refused only where it holds a test, cfg(test) or mod x; a doc fence is refused only where it is not a text block; eleven crates join the keep
decisions.why: This is the mechanism by which the covered run answers for the plain run wherever it actually does, which is what the task line asked. The plan measures each new admission (binaries read, fences listed, no integration tests, examples or benches).

decisions.summary: checks is excluded for its cfg(not(coverage)) test
decisions.why: The covered run genuinely does not run that test, so it does not answer for checks' plain run. The line's own scope is 'where the covered run answers'.

decisions.summary: rustc is excluded because its tests contain cfg(coverage) as text, which the conservative predicate refuses
decisions.why: A forgone saving, not a wrong outcome. T111's premise (no code reading cfg(coverage)) is applied as written, and nothing passes untested. This is a difference from the most a change could save, not a defect under XIV, and it narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: make rust-test is unchanged but for has_doctests, which now shares unit_tests_only's reading (holds_doctest), so the five text-only crates skip a cargo test --doc pass that ran no test
decisions.why: The constraint 'rust-test's fast uninstrumented loop unchanged' exists to keep the loop fast and uninstrumented, and it still is: no test stops running (all 10 fences are text, measured), and only an empty pass goes. A single reading keeps the keep and the run in agreement. This speeds the builders' loop, which FR-013 and the GM's perf priority cover.

decisions.summary: land's --all-features plain runs of pool, rust/mode_a and rust/phases are left
decisions.why: The coverage run (default features) does not answer for an --all-features cfg, so this falls outside 'where the covered run answers'.

decisions.id: D7a feature unification, T111's existing keep
decisions.summary: crates T111 already kept (owed, claims, land, trials) have covered tests run under unified features
decisions.why: Not T57's decision. It is T111's standing keep, reported as found and left, and no wrong outcome is shown.

decisions.id: D7b feature unification, rust/gate newly kept
decisions.summary: T57 adds rust/gate to the keep, though its covered tests may run with owed's testkit (which switches owed's entry_lines seam) while its own plain build lacks it
decisions.why: Here the covered run answers under unified features, not the crate's own. The bundle shows a difference but no wrong outcome: the gate (make done, the push) already rests on the coverage run alone for these crates, and the crate's lint runs on its own features. Under XIV, a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect, so leaving it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: no verdict key carries the environment; attributed to T93, not new with T57
decisions.why: The plain run's own key already has the same exposure, so the keep adds none. The tests T32 found were fixed. No new defect is left.

decisions.summary: the guard's refusal of the builder's Edit and Write in a kind:bg dispatcher's clone is filed as T62 rather than fixed here
decisions.why: A defect (a tool refusing valid work) that T57 leaves. The deferral meets FR-009: it says why it is not fixed here (the fix is in rust/guard's clone_sync_hooks, where T58 works in this clone, and a guard edit rebuilds the gate crates T58 is counting), names its filed id (T62) and gives its order (lands before T22, the close). So it is fixed within the feature, before the close.

decisions.id: T62-D1 parked_by as the backstop's third dispatcher source

decisions.id: D1 proceed past the task line's 'split only if hooks dominate'
decisions.summary: The split was built although hooks did not dominate on either measure: 246 of 520 non-test edits (47%) and 40 of the 85 edit-caused rebuilds, against 45 for the shared set. The 105 gate-used-guard and pylex edits move into l7r_shared with it, so 274 of 520 edits still rebuild everything.
decisions.why: The condition is not in request.md or the accepted spec. It comes from the task line, which the bundle only restates (item 2), and the block does not flag it as a departure, it just says 'so the split was built'. Taken literally the condition is NOT met. It was a test of whether the split pays, and a literal reading defeats that purpose and the GM's 'prioritize performance improvements' (FR-013: 'makes ... the builders' loop faster'). Without the split, every one of the 520 edits rebuilds 32 crates. With it, the 246 hook edits (the largest category) rebuild 1 crate (1.1-1.2 s against 11.6-50.8 s) and make rust-test owes only the guard and checks. The cost is measured and small: 33 crates instead of 32 on a shared edit, plus a second compile of l7r_shared under test-env on shared edits, which was not timed. The ruling does not rest on the work already being done.

decisions.id: D2 the rebuild-count red first is a one-shot measurement, with no standing pin (T66 per the dispatch)
decisions.summary: Item 9's 'red first' on the rebuild count is a before/after run of /tmp/t58/scripts/measure.sh, and nothing committed pins that a hook edit compiles one crate. The block does not mention the missing pin or T66.
decisions.why: The GM's request and the spec do not ask T58 for a standing pin. FR-012's red-first tests cover only the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013. The task line's 'red first on the rebuild count' is met in its words by a measured red (32 crates) and a measured green (1). A missing regression pin is not a wrong outcome (a defect, constitution XIV), so leaving it is within. The section should still list it under Found-and-left with its task id and order for the record, because the dispatch says T66 exists and that cannot be checked from the bundle. This is a note, not a block.

decisions.id: D3 make-only's refusal of a read-only Python heredoc left to T63

The accepted spec's FR-009 sets the terms for a deferral, and the block meets all three: why it is not fixed here (it is make-only's reading of a heredoc, not the split, and needs its own measurement and red first), the filed id (T63), and the order ('lands before T22', the close). It is fixed inside this feature before the close, and it blocks nothing in the meantime because it passes under a recorded escape.

decisions.id: D4 test-env feature and its double compile judged 'not a defect'
decisions.summary: The guard's tests reach l7r_shared's test seams through a dev-dependency-only feature. In crate-a-call builds l7r_shared compiles twice, and a --workspace call could, in principle, give a gate binary the test thread's map.
decisions.why: Against the wrong-outcome definition: no lane makes the one call that unifies test-env into a gate binary. Shipped binaries are built '--profile tool -p', and the tool fingerprint shows features [] (measured). The double compile is a cost on l7r_shared edits only, and nothing works wrongly because of it. No defect is left.

decisions.summary: This is how the split is done.

decisions.id: D6 the guard-file patterns follow the move (guard_file_hooks, make_only GUARD_FILE and SOURCE_NAMES)

decisions.why: Without this the moved guard sources would lose their protection, which would be a defect the split introduced. It is pinned red-first by two tests.

decisions.id: D7 hookbench's baseline also finds a guard under rust/guard/shared/src/guards/
decisions.summary: This fixes a break the split caused, pinned by a y-hooks case.
decisions.why: It fixes a defect the step itself introduced, as fix-as-we-go asks.

decisions.id: D8 edits outside the brief's listed surface: docs, research/blocked-domains.json, scripts/hooks/lib, tests/hooks, rust/mode_a, browser, embed
decisions.summary: Every reader of a moved path is updated so that it keeps working.
decisions.why: Each one was judged on its own. docs and scripts/hooks/lib appear in the block's text: the guardlog.sh and failed-open-log.sh comments, and 'the docs follow the move'. rust/mode_a, browser and embed appear as dependents whose manifests and paths now name l7r_shared. tests/hooks and research/blocked-domains.json do not appear in the bundle, so they are classed on the dispatch's description (a moved path's reader) and are unverified. decisions.id: D9 apply via git apply --3way after T57/T62 landed, conflict kept with T62's words; make format over 24 dependents
decisions.summary: Integration and formatting only.
decisions.why: Nothing that was asked is changed. The rustfmt joins come from the shorter paths.

decisions.summary: feature-report shows where-time's columns through one reader (where_time::columns_text), in process, its UNTIL= kept, in a section after the session's time; each agent's own row left to make where-time
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask that feature-report read the same columns through the same functions in one place and keep its UNTIL=. One shared reader is exactly that. The report carries every column FR-005 names: the critical path apart from the summed agent-minutes, the tokens, and the rework. Each agent's span and tokens under its task are still read by the same function and shown by make where-time, so no reading is lost or forked.

decisions.summary: the window feature-report passes is its own, first event to last when no SINCE/UNTIL is given
decisions.why: This fixes a wrong outcome found in building. With both empty, the report counted every feature's turn lines: 6,900 min of critical path against the window's 1,417 (labeled 2026-11-21). A report of this feature's time that counts other features' time is a defect, and the fix serves FR-005. The small token and agent-minute gap against where-time is the same reader over a window that opens seconds later. That is a difference, not a defect, and no exactness standard applies.

decisions.summary: plan re-rounds are a later round of one review on one subject, keyed by agent and MANIFEST subject (feature_report::tables::round_key), booked to the task its line names else the mark, the all row counting every one; spec-fidelity-verify not keyed separately because the hook logs a routed later round under spec-fidelity
decisions.why: The approved improvement 4 ('Fewer plan re-rounds') and FR-005 ('count the rework (... plan re-rounds)') mean a review sent back for another round. The first wording counted first-round reviews of different block bundles: 68 against 23 (the Measured table, labeled). That overstated the column it named and was a defect. The restated key measures what was asked and drops no re-round. An untasked one goes to the mark row and the all row counts all of them. A routed verify round is logged under spec-fidelity (none of the 451 log's 108 under the twin's name, measured 2026-11-21). A hand-dispatched verify is a spec round with no MANIFEST, so it is not a plan re-round.

decisions.summary: a spec-fidelity dispatch inside the window is a re-round when any earlier dispatch in the feature's log holds its key, inside the window or before SINCE; the log before SINCE is read a second time where SINCE is given
decisions.why: This is the correction the last verdict asked for, in its own words. A second round run inside the window is counted as that window's rework, whether its first round fell before SINCE or not. It is red first: a_re_round_inside_the_window_counts_a_first_round_before_since read 0 against 2 before the fix. It is measured on a SINCE that cuts a subject: 6 -> 7 between T44's second and third rounds, labeled 2026-11-21, with command. T10's bounds are unchanged at 23 because that SINCE cuts nothing. It narrows nothing. The second read's cost (about 0.25 to 0.35 s, labeled with load) is a cost, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: feature-report's existing rounds table stays counted inside the window and says so under its heading, rather than being re-read across SINCE like the re-rounds column
decisions.why: The rounds table is feature-report's existing table, and the request and spec ask nothing of it. FR-005's rework count is the plan re-rounds column, which now counts correctly across SINCE. The last verdict named labeling the table as one of the two acceptable remedies, and the label does what that remedy was for. The table and the column count two stated things, so they no longer disagree silently, and a reader is never told a wrong number. Where SINCE cuts no subject they agree (23 = 23 and 25 = 25, the Measured table). The report passes its own first event as SINCE where none is given, so for the default report the two read the same. Leaving an unrequested existing table as it is, with an honest heading, is a difference, not a defect (XIV v2.36.0). So it is within and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: an agent is booked to its first stop's task (the agent's meta file, D6), else its first start's, because before 451 T53's landing a start line carried the clone's active task (57 of 164 agents with both; 0 of 22 since), red first
decisions.why: D7 puts each agent's span and tokens 'under its task', and D6 takes the stop line's task from the agent's meta file. Booking 57 agents to the clone's active mark was a wrong outcome: T15's plan reviews read under T18 (measured 2026-11-21 with method). The fix-as-we-go ruling (2026-11-18) says a step fixes the defects it finds. The fix only changes which recorded field the requested column reads, choosing the one D6 already names. It is red first and changes nothing for agents started after T53.

decisions.summary: A new text check, l7r-gate check guard-deps, run by make static after the conflict check, refusing a manifest that names l7r_guard and naming l7r_shared with its path and rust/guard/shared for guard-only pieces.
decisions.why: It is the task as filed (a check in make static, refusing a dependency on l7r_guard, naming l7r_shared). It is a guard whose only reach is the regression it pins, T58's one-crate rebuild, and it is performance work under FR-013.

decisions.summary: Walk every Cargo.toml under rust/ on disk (target and hidden directories and symlinks not walked), not git-listed, because the workspace's gate/crates/* glob builds untracked crates too.
decisions.why: The filed scope is manifests under rust/, which holds the workspace whose rebuild count T58 measured. Walking the disk rather than git's list widens the reach to untracked crates the glob builds, so nothing is narrowed. Item 4 records a grep showing no manifest under tests/ or scripts/ names the guard.

decisions.summary: Only the guard's own manifest is exempt.
decisions.why: The task line exempts the binaries that ship the guard. Item 4 records that l7r-guard.sh and hookbench build it with -p l7r_guard and no dependency, and cargo tree -i shows no dependent, so the guard's own manifest is the whole of that exemption. The exemption is exactly as large as the filed one, no larger.

decisions.summary: Forms read: a key in any dependency table (normal, dev, build, target, workspace; - and _ alike; dotted or quoted keys), a [*dependencies.l7r_guard] table, a rename through package, and comments cut at #. A path-only dependency under another key is not read, because cargo refuses one (measured probe); the check looks at direct dependencies only.
decisions.why: The forms come from Cargo's manifest format. The one form left out cannot build: the probe records cargo refusing it ('no matching package named hooks'), so leaving it out is not a carve-out. Any transitive dependency needs some manifest under rust/ to name the guard directly, and the check refuses that manifest, so checking direct dependencies alone loses nothing of the purpose.

decisions.summary: Record each run as check-guard-deps and add its entry to scripts/tool-registry.json, because check tool-signals went red without it.
decisions.why: This is the project's existing rule for a recorded tool, and the entry is needed for the requested check to pass hooks-test. It enforces the request and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: The second make closing-checks run went red only at rust lint, on T65's in-flight set_down_hooks.rs. T65's file is left alone, guard-deps run alone passed, and one green make closing-checks is recorded as owed once T65's file lints clean.
decisions.why: This is sequencing, not scope: the green exit is still required and is recorded as owed, not waived, and the failing file belongs to another task in flight. No requirement of the request or of FR-013 is dropped.

decisions.summary: Classed [perf] under FR-013, and not engine speed, so no performance-checklist answers.
decisions.why: FR-013 covers work that makes the builders' loop faster. A pin that keeps T58's hook-edit rebuild at 1 crate against 32 protects exactly that, and the GM asked for performance work in general to come first.

decisions.summary: running reads the transcript once, in order, line at a time; each line's events sorted by place; an id's last word kept (launched/resumed/interim), a final notice or stop drops it
decisions.why: T65's line as filed: the transcript read in order, an agent's last launch or resume after its last notification running. This is that rule, implemented.

decisions.summary: a SendMessage resume is read from resumedAgentId in the tool's own record, as LAUNCHED's third key
decisions.why: T65's line: a resume after a notice reads as running; the key's shape is measured from a real transcript (153 records).

decisions.summary: an interim notice ends nothing by itself; an agent whose last word is interim runs while its own transcript holds its own work running, an interim sub-agent (cycle-guarded), or a wake since its last turn's end - not the literal 'interim never final'
decisions.why: Narrows the dispatch's 'an interim notice is not final' read literally (neither request.md nor the spec says interim is never final). The literal reading defeats the purpose of the Stop hook's test FR-013 relies on (set_down_hooks.rs): 8 agents never notified again, so the guard would be silent from line 2,132 of 50,891 for the rest of the session, 32 wrong turn ends (measured 2026-11-21, sim.py/stops.py). The adopted reading still treats an interim notice as non-final - running-ness is decided by the agent's own work - and its replay agrees with the approximate truth at all 1,868 turn ends. The plan states the departure openly under 'Why not the literal rule'.

decisions.summary: a turn's end is read from the end_turn record holding the text block, not any end_turn record (the thinking record carries end_turn first)
decisions.why: Makes the interim reading correct on a measured case (a4e93c6a, 19 s gap); no scope beyond the task's reader.

decisions.summary: the interim agents' own transcripts are read only when the parent's read leaves nothing plainly running
decisions.why: The guard's question is whether anything runs; skipping the second read when something plainly runs changes no verdict and costs 45-70 ms less (measured). Within the performance-first rule FR-013.

decisions.summary: an interim agent with no transcript of its own reads not running, as before
decisions.why: Keeps existing behavior on a case measured to be correct (the first of the 8 never-notified agents, line 2,132, has no transcript and never ran again); not a defect left.

decisions.summary: api-request-blob lines are not read, since they re-emit old notices that would end a resumed agent
decisions.why: Required for the ordered reading to be correct; measured that no task-id appears only in a blob across 12 transcripts, so no notice is lost.

decisions.summary: a background Bash run's launch and notice read as before; T66 and T11 left alone
decisions.why: The dispatch's constraint and the task's scope; no request clause is dropped.

decisions.summary: five tests red first (4 failed, the no-file case passed, pinning kept behavior); the thinking-record assertion added with the turn-end fix and not run red; a temporary real-transcript acceptance test removed before the closing checks
decisions.why: T65's line asks red first on a resume after a notice, which was run red. FR-012's red-first rule covers the refusals of FR-006-FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, and a Stop-hook reading fix is not one of those refusals, so the one assertion not run red narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: T65 classed as performance work ([perf], FR-013): keeps the builders' loop running unrefused; no performance-checklist answers since not engine speed
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the builders' loop faster as performance work; a Stop hook that wrongly refuses turns while builders run slows that loop.

decisions.summary: nothing found and left
decisions.why: The final replay leaves no wrong turn end against the approximate truth; no defect is deferred.

decisions.summary: The re-file deletes its own parse of task-starts.jsonl, its in_force and its started, and calls the writer's (filed.rs starts/in_force/started/Start, made public). The writer's behavior is unchanged.
decisions.why: The re-file and the writer filing a line by one rule is what makes make where-time book each line to the feature it served (FR-005, the tooling request: make the retrospective cheap to put together going forward). The 23 lines in 385's log, a feature with no T47, are a wrong outcome: 451's reading leaves out three of T47's reviews. So this is a defect fix, not a difference.

decisions.summary: The re-file hands the writer's functions only the starts made by the line's time (with START_SLACK), and the line's t as now, so a start's age is measured as it was when the line was written.
decisions.why: It applies the writer's rule as the writer applied it when it wrote the line, which is how the two are made to agree. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Shares the writer's next link too. Where no start in force names the task, the line goes to feature.json as it stood at the line's time, read as the feature of the clone's last start by then. It moves only where that feature has the task, and is marked "fallback": true as the writer marks it. This is a labeled CONVENTION, because feature.json keeps no history.
decisions.why: It was measured that sharing the stale-start rule alone moves none of the 23, so this is what the task's goal takes, not a carve-out from it. The convention's limit, that a make claim between two starts is not seen, comes from having no history to read, not from a choice to cover less. It is bounded by the has-the-task test. For the 23 the result is backed by an independent source, the dispatchers' descriptions. No requirement is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The dispatcher's brief is not made the re-file's rule, because the writer has no such step.
decisions.why: Keeping one rule for writer and re-file is the section's stated goal, and a rule only the re-file had would bring back the disagreement this task removes. It is a design choice inside what was asked.

decisions.summary: The run's summary counts fallback moves apart and prints that count only when it is nonzero.
decisions.why: A reporting detail of the re-file's own output. It serves reading what moved and why, and takes nothing from any FR.

decisions.summary: One edit past the file list: event_log_hooks.rs's pub use widened to the four names, run through make guard-edit.
decisions.why: Only makes the shared rule visible, with no change in behavior. It is declared and went through the guard.

decisions.summary: No reader reads the fallback mark, though T53's section says readers keep a marked line apart (grep, measured 2026-11-21). Left, raised with the coordinator.
decisions.why: No FR asks for a fallback mark or for readers to keep one apart. That line is T53's claim, so leaving it narrows no requirement or request clause. By the defect standard (constitution XIV v2.36.0) no wrong outcome is shown: the 23 are booked to the right task, and a wrong booking elsewhere is unshown. A claim the code does not match, where the behavior is fine, is fixed by restating the claim, and that is T53's text, not T56's files. Aside for the coordinator: T53's sentence wants restating, or a reader built if a mis-booking is ever shown.

decisions.summary: T56 is classed as [perf] performance work under FR-013.
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words count measurement work, the event log's data and make where-time's readers, as performance work for ordering. Filing each line in the right feature's log is that data's correctness.

decisions.summary: Exits: the red case green with the earlier test unedited, crate checks, closing-checks, the dry run before and after. Red: recorded, set down, a can't-be-done claim taken to arbiter-ask. Order: after T53 and T58, before T22.
decisions.why: Process and ordering inside the feature's own scheme. No requirement is narrowed.

decisions.summary: fields::agent_cost re-reads the growing transcript every 5 ms (REPLY_POLL) while the payload's last_assistant_message is not yet the last assistant row's text since the last user row, so tok counts the reply
decisions.why: Makes the stop line carry the agent's token cost as D6 defines it (the transcript's sum, each message.id once) - FR-004 and the 2026-11-19 approval's idea 4. The cause is measured (60 of 83 stops short by exactly the reply; the probe shows the reply lands 5.8-89.2 ms into the hook), and fixing the writer instead of restating the claim follows from the measurement that the reply is readable during the hook.

decisions.summary: The wait is bounded at 1 s (REPLY_WAIT, ten times the probe's latest landing); past it the writer records what is on disk, as before
decisions.why: A Stop-hook writer that never refuses has to terminate; the bound covers every reply observed by a factor of ten, so FR-004's cost is recorded in every observed case, and the residue (a reply later than 1 s) is a design tolerance, not a case the plan excludes from what was asked. It also keeps the per-stop cost small, consistent with FR-013's priority on the builders' loop speed.

decisions.summary: ctx is read after the wait, so it is the reply's context rather than one call stale
decisions.why: D6 says ctx is the agent's last call's context; the stale ctx on the same 60 stops is the same defect, fixed together.

decisions.summary: A payload with no reply text or no readable transcript waits for nothing; a stop with no readable transcript still writes neither tok nor ctx, and the hook never refuses
decisions.why: Unchanged behavior, and the 4 such stops measured have no transcript anywhere, so there is nothing to sum; FR-004 is not narrowed by declining to invent a figure that cannot be read.

decisions.summary: The 10,370 stop lines written before the field existed are explained (they predate T07) and are not backfilled
decisions.why: T59's own question was why most stops lack tok; the measured answer is their date. FR-004 is about the stop line the writer records, and SC-002 asks for reproducibility for work done after the feature lands, so no backfill was requested.

decisions.summary: Only fields.rs and its tests change; T56's refile.rs and T64's order.rs are left alone; where-time and feature-report readers unchanged because T10 already takes the transcript's sum first
decisions.why: Sequencing and file ownership, not a reduction of any requirement; the readers already satisfy FR-005 for cost, and the log's own record is the part fixed.

decisions.summary: Red-first test, crate-scoped rust-test/lint/cover/format on rust/guard/shared, then make closing-checks; after landing, compare.py/gap.py check the next stops
decisions.why: Verification of FR-004 as asked, using the crate-scoped loop the GM approved (improvement 2); enforcement of the requested behavior, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Filed and scheduled as a [perf] task
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work on the event log's data as performance work for ordering (the GM 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task').

decisions.summary: The order notice skips an edit once its own task has a landing after it in the log (keyed on the edit's task), not keyed on the decide's task and not on the decide's task's landing-else-first-start
decisions.why: A fix to a wrong outcome (constitution XIV): the main session was told about a Makefile edit that had landed hours before, which teaches it to ignore the notice. The block measured that keying on the decide's task drops none of the 22 wrong firings (127 -> 127), so it would not fix the defect. The start-based reading also drops 2 right firings (a builder's unlanded edit made before its task's first start). Keying on the edit's task removes exactly the 22, all on landed edits, and keeps every unlanded builder edit, which is the notice's job under FR-013's builders' loop. This is the fix that does what it says it is for; it narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: 'Landed' reuses static_runs_hooks' rule: a Phase end line with landed true whose tasks names the task, whatever its exit code
decisions.why: Reuses one existing definition rather than a second one; it decides how the fix is built, not what was asked.

decisions.summary: Landing lines are not filtered by caller, so the main session's make land lands a builder's edits of its tasks
decisions.why: Measured: all 21 landings in 451's log are the main session's lines, so filtering by caller would leave every builder edit unlanded forever and keep the defect for builders. Needed for the fix to work.

decisions.summary: An edit with no task is never skipped and counts as before
decisions.why: Keeps T55's behavior where no landing can name the edit; measured 127 such lines, all from 2026-11-20 04h-06h before edits carried a task, so nothing current is affected. Borrowing the decide's task would guess; leaving them as they were narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D1 the cap reads the builder's own last message iteration
decisions.summary: usage_of reads input, cache read and cache creation from the last usage.iterations entry of type message, and context() (the cap's reader) goes through it, instead of the top-level sum that adds both of the builder's own iterations around an advisor call
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a builder's call once ITS context is past the threshold. Item 4 measured that on every one of the 581 advisor rows the top level is the sum of the builder's two own iterations (about twice its context), that the advisor's iteration is a separate model's, and that the builder's next call read 152,979 after a 300,884 top level. Reading the doubled sum refused 33 builders at 151k to 290k, well under the 300k knob: that is a wrong outcome against FR-006 and request improvement 1 (keep builder contexts small, not stop them at half), so fixing the reader makes the requirement do what it says. No exception is made.

decisions.summary: the top level is read only where the row has no iterations list, no message entry, or an own iteration of zero
decisions.why: Item 4 measured 6 rows with no list. On those, and on the single-iteration rows (27,506), the top level is the builder's own context, so the fallback keeps the existing correct reading where there is nothing else to read. It narrows nothing FR-006 asks.

decisions.summary: the 300k constant stays; only how it is read changes
decisions.why: FR-006 sets the knob at 300k (GUESS, tuned from FR-004's data) and nothing in the request or spec asks to move it with this fix. Leaving it means a builder now meets the cap FR-006 actually states.

decisions.id: D4 the event log's ctx fixed by the same change
decisions.summary: ctx calls context(), so it now records the builder's own context on an advisor row rather than the doubled sum
decisions.why: ctx is the per-call context figure FR-004/FR-005's readers and FR-006's tuning depend on ('the knob tuned from FR-004's data'). The same doubled read was a wrong figure; fixing it with the one shared reader serves the request's measurement half.

decisions.id: D5 tok keeps the billed top level
decisions.summary: call_of, the event log's cost figure, keeps the top-level sum, because both of the builder's own iterations are billed; the parse is shared through message_of
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for an agent's token cost. Both own iterations are billed calls, so their sum is the builder's own cost. Leaving tok on the top level keeps that correct, rather than carrying the context fix into a figure where it would be wrong.

decisions.id: D6 the advisor's own tokens left out of tok, deferred to T69

decisions.summary: The fix's scope is set by a replay of the whole make-only guard log (286 refusals, 250 still standing; each still-refused program re-judged with its body blanked), finding 4 read-only programs among the refusals
decisions.why: T63's line asks to measure first which refusals were of read-only scripts; this is that measurement, labeled with date and method, and its partition (155+21+4 refusals of the 250, 196 refused rows with no Python program across refusals and escapes) is internally consistent.

decisions.summary: The fix goes in py_c alone, the one judge of whether a Python program writes; make_only_hooks.rs and interp.rs untouched
decisions.why: Where the fix lives decides nothing about what passes; the line asks that a read-only heredoc pass, and fixing the judge that misread it does exactly that.

decisions.summary: An f-string argv element of the form --name={value}, the name literal and the value holding no ( ) \ $ or line break, is judged as the literal option --name=_; writes_flag still judges it by its name, so writing options (--output=, --out=, --ext-diff=, grep's --filter=) stay writes
decisions.why: This is the mechanism that makes the one measured read-only heredoc not importing tree code (T58's, 2026-11-21T05:51:53Z) pass, which the line asks for; the writing-option names staying refused keeps the line's own condition (opens no file for writing). The placeholder _ is sound because writes_flag reads only the option name.

decisions.summary: f-string elements whose option name or effect py_c cannot know stay a write: a call, escape or $ in the value, short options, a field in the name (f'--{o}={x}'), no = (f'--since{x}', which a field can complete into another option name), a git global option before the subcommand, an option as the command, a writing subcommand
decisions.why: Read literally, the line ('a heredoc that opens no file for writing passes') would also pass a read-only program written in these shapes, so keeping them refused narrows it. But a static judge cannot tell that such an element writes nothing: a call in the value can itself open a file for writing (the plan's own {open("Makefile", "w")} case), and a field in or right after the option name can render to a writing option. Passing them would let writes through, which defeats the guard the GM asked to be real enforcement (2026-11-19). The measured log holds no read-only refusal of these shapes (the 4 read-only programs are all accounted for), so the narrowing costs no measured case.

decisions.summary: The 3 programs of 2026-11-21T01:55:09Z (twice) and 01:55:10Z (T42's replay), which open nothing for writing in their own text but put scripts/ on sys.path and import _hm_house, the tree's own code, stay refused
decisions.why: These are refusals of programs whose own text opens nothing for writing, so the line read literally would pass them. But the line's condition is that the program opens no file for writing, and a program that imports tree code runs that code, which py_c does not read and which can be edited to write anything, a guard file included. So the condition cannot be established for these programs. Passing them would also open a direct bypass of the make-only guard: put the write in an importable helper and import it. That defeats the purpose of the guard the line refines, and the GM asked on 2026-11-19 that enforcement be real enforcement, not instructions. Refusing what cannot be judged is the guard's designed behavior, not a check refusing known-good work, so this leaves no defect behind. One episode (3 rows, one replay) is affected, and it can still take the existing recorded escape.

decisions.summary: Red first on T58's heredoc verbatim (unit test and make-only suite case, both failing before, passing after), plus 18 refuse cases and a --output= suite twin pinned as writes before and after
decisions.why: The line asks for red first on the refused script's shape. The pins only enforce that the change passes nothing that writes, which serves the request (enforcement, not new behavior).

decisions.summary: Done is measured by replaying the whole guard log on the new binary and comparing it row by row with the replay before T63: exactly one row (T58's) flips, refused to passed, and no writing, shell-refused, non-Python or tree-importing row changes
decisions.why: This verifies that the change does what the line asks and nothing more; it adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: A python -c program reaches py_c the same way as a heredoc and is read by the same rule
decisions.why: It is the same judge reading the same program text. The line names a heredoc as the measured case, not as an exclusion, and a -c program that opens no file for writing is the same thing in another shape.

decisions.summary: Before writer-alive.sh says gone it asks l7r-guard --finished-run alive, which uses the existing /proc walk (by pid, never by pattern) to find a live process outside the asker's ancestry whose command line or started script text writes the file (>, >>, >|, &>, tee).
decisions.why: This is what T61's line asks (ask the run's own process through finished_run_hooks' /proc walk, red first on a quiet log over a live run) and what its second brief asks (count only a process whose text WRITES the file). It serves FR-013 [perf] and the 2026-11-19 approval of the builders'-loop improvements.

decisions.id: T61-2 readers are no proof of life
decisions.summary: A process that only names the file (a Monitor tail -f | grep in a bash -c wrapper, an until [ -s f ] wait) is not life; reader arguments (READERS) are never read as scripts; the held-open answer counts only a descriptor opened for writing (fdinfo flags), replacing fuser -s.
decisions.why: Fixes a defect the task found (a reader held a dead run's wait to its 90-minute ceiling, measured red first in round 2); it is the second brief's 'two reader shapes pinned dead'.

decisions.id: T61-3 non-redirect writers still read gone
decisions.summary: A run that writes without shell redirection or tee (Python open(), sort -o) still reads gone once 45 s quiet; parsing each language's writes priced and not built.
decisions.why: It narrows the brief's 'a process whose text WRITES the file' to shell writes. Ruled on purpose: the only way to count such writers without parsing every language is to count a process that names the file, and the task measured that this keeps dead waits alive to the 90-minute ceiling, which defeats the purpose. The shape left behaves as it did before T61, and none of the 8 measured false firings had it, so no observed wrong outcome is left behind. A shape with no measured instance is not a known defect that FR-009 would make the plan file.

decisions.id: T61-4 phases.log waits deferred to T71
decisions.summary: The 2 of 8 false firings on phases.log (an agent appending from separate foreground calls, no process between them) still read gone; filed as T71, lands before T22.

Dropping the rm -f is a consequence (a new directory has no stale files).
